text:
anya: quick follow-up to the lazy-shard routing RFC thread — I sketched a practical hybrid: default lazy-on-demand shard fetch + optional eager warmup for routes we detect as latency-sensitive (canary/paid tiers). thoughts?

mike: sounds reasonable. how do you plan to detect latency-sensitive routes? per-route config? heuristics?

anya: both. per-route opt-in for customers + heuristic scoring (recent p50/p95, token rates, error spikes). heuristics feed into an autosuggest in console.

sam: main tradeoff is memory vs cold-start latency. lazy keeps mem low but first requests hit disk/network. eager costs memory but avoids cold spikes. need eviction policy for eager buffers.

anya: agreed. my draft: eager warmup only for routes with >100 RPS sustained or explicit pin. otherwise lazy. eviction: LRU with age+score decay, and priority buckets for pinned shards.

mike: nit: consider shard granularity for eager — some models have tiny shards (few MB) others are large. warmup policy should be shard-size-aware so we don't thrash.

anya: yes — plan includes a cost model: expected latency reduction per shard / memory footprint -> score. threshold tunable.

nate: what about safetensors + contiguous sharding vs chunked tarballs? warmup will behave differently. for safetensors slices we can mmap portions if FS supports it. for tarballs we need prefetch extractor.

anya: good point. propose a WeightSource abstraction with two capabilities: streamable (can read chunk-by-chunk) and mmappable. router picks strategy per source type.

sam: also need to handle cross-shard attention cases where activation fetches multiple shards simultaneously. warmup should try to co-locate frequently co-requested shards. maybe a co-access graph and group warmups.

anya: co-access graph is nice but adds complexity. initial version: heuristic grouping by model-namespace + adjacent shard ids for sharded layouts produced by our packer. follow-up RFC for co-access clustering.

mike: metrics to drive heuristics? we should emit shard-level metrics: fetch-latency, fetch-count, post-warmup hit-rate, memory-evictions. then ML job suggests warmup candidates.

anya: yes — add telemetry points. also add an opt-out data capture flag for customers.

nate: fallback story? if eager warmup fails (OOM on node), we should gracefully fallback to lazy fetch and mark that route as ineligible until admin intervention.

anya: agreed. plan: try-eager with reservation accounting; on OOM revert and add a cooldown + alert. also allow per-customer hard cap.

sam: what about safety with safetensors index vs manifest v2? the loader must validate checksums and support partial manifests for huge models. partial manifests let us warmup just a subset.

anya: implemented in the draft: manifest v2 supports shard-level checksums + byte ranges. loader can request only ranges needed for warmup. supports both safetensors-index and tarball manifests.

mike: rollout plan? canary on dedicated cluster first then hosted. flag gated by route config + infra toggle.

anya: yep. rollout steps in RFC follow-up doc: feature-flag, canary small customer set, observe metrics for 2 weeks, then staged enable. I'll open tracking ticket.

infra-bot: deploy: warmup-agent v0.1 canary started on cluster-redwood-canary-3 at 2024-11-05T08:23:01Z :rocket:

nate: action items: (1) anya to add WeightSource capability enum + small API sketch, (2) mike to add shard-level telemetry events, (3) sam to prototype LRU+priority eviction sim. due EOD next Thu.

anya: adding API sketch to the RFC doc now. will ping when ready. thanks all :heart:
